name: Database testing
note: Questions authored by Claude as practice material. Not sourced from your own notes or any official exam. Verify anything you doubt against the docs.

questions.q: Which query finds duplicate cms_id values?
options: SELECT cms_id FROM t WHERE COUNT(*) > 1
SELECT cms_id, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY cms_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
SELECT cms_id FROM t ORDER BY cms_id
questions.why: Group, then filter groups with HAVING. Aggregates are not allowed in WHERE.

questions.q: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING?
options: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation
questions.why: Order of evaluation: WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING.

questions.q: Find child rows whose parent_id points to no existing parent. Which pattern?
options: INNER JOIN parent ... WHERE p.id IS NOT NULL
LEFT JOIN parent p ON c.parent_id = p.id WHERE p.id IS NULL
questions.why: A LEFT JOIN keeps children with no match; the NULL parent id exposes orphans.

questions.q: Which condition correctly finds rows where config is missing?
questions.why: Comparing with = NULL is never true. Use IS NULL.

questions.q: What does COUNT(col) do differently from COUNT(*)?
options: COUNT(col) skips rows where col is NULL
questions.why: COUNT(col) ignores NULLs; COUNT(*) counts every row.

questions.q: What does an INNER JOIN return?
options: All rows from the left table
Only rows with a match in both tables
questions.why: Unmatched rows on either side are dropped.

questions.q: Why can NOT IN (subquery) return no rows when the subquery contains a NULL?
options: It is a bug in the database
Comparisons with NULL are unknown, so no row can satisfy NOT IN
It only happens with text columns
questions.why: Use NOT EXISTS or filter NULLs out of the subquery.

questions.q: Which expression numbers duplicates within each cms_id so you can pick the extra copies?
options: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cms_id ORDER BY id)
questions.why: ROW_NUMBER restarts per partition; rows numbered above 1 are duplicates.

questions.q: For checks run against a shared test environment, what is the safest practice?
options: Use an admin account for speed
Run SELECT-only queries, ideally with a read-only database user
questions.why: Checks should observe, never modify, data other people rely on.

questions.q: In PostgreSQL, which expression reads a JSON field as text so you can test it for NULL? (assumes PostgreSQL)
questions.why: ->> returns text; ->  returns json. Confirm your actual database engine before using.

questions.q: What does SELECT do?
questions.why: SELECT retrieves data.

questions.q: What does ORDER BY do?
questions.why: Add DESC for descending order.

questions.q: What does LIMIT 10 do?
questions.why: It caps the number of returned rows. (PostgreSQL and MySQL syntax.)

questions.q: What is a primary key?
options: A column that uniquely identifies each row
questions.why: It must be unique and not null.

questions.q: What is a foreign key?
options: A column that references the primary key of another table
questions.why: It links rows between tables and can enforce referential integrity.

questions.q: How does a LEFT JOIN differ from an INNER JOIN?
options: LEFT keeps all left rows even without a match
questions.why: Unmatched right-side columns come back as NULL.

questions.q: What does GROUP BY category_id with COUNT(*) return?
options: The number of rows for each category_id
questions.why: One output row per group.

questions.q: What does SELECT DISTINCT name do?
questions.why: It only affects the result, not stored data.

questions.q: Is BETWEEN 1 AND 5 inclusive?
questions.why: 1 and 5 both match.

questions.q: What does LIKE 'abc%' match?
options: Strings containing abc only in the middle
questions.why: % matches any run of characters.

questions.q: What does COALESCE(a, 'n/a') return?
questions.why: Useful for readable reports with NULLs.

questions.q: UNION vs UNION ALL:
options: UNION removes duplicate rows; UNION ALL keeps them
questions.why: UNION ALL skips the dedupe step.

questions.q: Why can EXISTS be preferable to IN with a subquery that may return NULL?
options: It tests for matching rows and is not tripped up by NULLs the way NOT IN is
questions.why: NOT EXISTS is the safe form for anti-joins.

questions.q: What is a CTE (WITH clause) good for?
options: Naming a subquery so a complex query reads in steps
questions.why: It improves readability and allows recursion.

questions.q: How do you walk a parent_id chain of unknown depth in SQL?
questions.why: WITH RECURSIVE follows parent to child (or back) until no rows remain.

questions.q: What does EXPLAIN show?
options: The query plan the database intends to use
questions.why: EXPLAIN ANALYZE also runs the query and shows real timing.

questions.q: Which database feature stops duplicate cms_id values from being inserted at all?
questions.why: Constraints enforce the rule at write time; checks only detect violations afterwards.

questions.q: Your sync check reads the database one second after a webhook fires and sometimes finds old data. What is the most reliable fix?
options: Poll with a short interval and a timeout until the expected row appears
Run it twice and take the better result
questions.why: Sync is asynchronous, so wait on a condition, not on a fixed delay.
